widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the speaking person in <Picture 1>: same facial identity, geometry, apparent age, skin tone, Short, dark black textured tousled hair with a soft fringe over the forehead., body and shoulder proportions.
<Subject 2> is the wardrobe in <Picture 1>: Off-white long-sleeve henley shirt with partial button placket and notched neckline, smooth knit texture. A small black lavalier microphone is clipped to the shirt's image-right collar area. Preserve the visible garment layers, colors, sleeve and collar shapes, patterns, logos, and worn accessories in their original positions.
<Subject 3> is the environment and visible objects in <Picture 1>: Blurred indoor scene with bright overhead ceiling lights, out-of-focus yellow and green colored displays, and brown-toned lower structural elements, lit with soft ambient lighting. Visible object inventory: One brown shopping cart handle with silver end components positioned at the bottom of the frame.. Preserve the exact count, visible contents, and positions in every frame. Preserve the background landmarks, object count, and left-to-right layout; add no objects or contents absent from <Picture 1>.
<Subject 4> is the performance in <Video 1>: subtle expression, gaze, blinking, and head rhythm only.
<Picture 1> is the visual source for identity, wardrobe, environment, lighting, framing, shot size, and colors.
<Video 1> supplies gaze, blinking, subtle non-speaking expressions and minor head movement only; <Picture 1> remains the visual anchor.
<Audio 1> is the sole speech timing reference for <Subject 1> (S1): spoken words, phonemes, pauses, and mouth/jaw articulation.

summary:
[reference generation] One continuous static talking shot. <Subject 1> speaks in sync with <Audio 1>; the visible outfit, background layout, lighting and composition stay as in <Picture 1> throughout.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - facial identity, visible hair, skin tone and body proportions.
<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - garment layers, colors, shapes, logos and worn accessories remain the same in every frame.
<Subject 3> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - background landmarks and visible objects keep their positions, count and contents.
<Subject 4> (appears in [Shot 1]): partially_preserved - natural facial expression follows the delivery of <Audio 1>.
<Picture 1> ([Shot 1]): fully_preserved - original framing, crop, subject scale, headroom, background alignment and colors stay constant.
<Video 1> (performance reference): weak_reference - use gaze, blinking, subtle non-speaking expressions and minor head motion only; <Picture 1> supplies appearance and framing, and <Audio 1> supplies speech timing.
<Audio 1>: reference - its spoken content, phonemes and pauses drive target speech and lip/jaw articulation.

detailed_description:
The target video shows <Subject 1> speaking to camera in the same visible lighting and setting as <Picture 1>. The frame holds <Subject 1>, <Subject 2>, and <Subject 3> exactly as in <Picture 1>, with nothing added to the scene.
[Shot 1] Hold one continuous shot with zero camera movement. The original framing, crop, character-to-camera distance and scale remain consistent with <Picture 1> throughout; mouth movement occurs only during audible speech in <Audio 1>, while blinking and breathing may continue through the final frame.

OPENING:
At frame 0 of every segment, match the visible composition of <Picture 1>: apparent subject scale and position, visible body extent, headroom, and background landmarks that remain inside the output frame. This opening composition is the reference for every subsequent frame, including the middle and final frame; only lip-sync, blinking, subtle breathing, minor head rotations, subtle expression, and small permitted gestures change. Match the identity, visible outfit, background layout, and lighting of <Picture 1>.

CAMERA AND COMPOSITION LOCK:
STATIC TRIPOD LOCK: Use one fixed camera position, lens field of view, and crop for the entire segment. The person occupies the same portion of the output frame at the opening, midpoint, and final frame, while the same visible background landmarks keep their relative positions. Hold this relationship continuously between those moments: no sudden or gradual zoom, push-in, digital crop, subject enlargement, or reframing. ACOUSTIC STRESS LOCK: Vocal emphasis may change lip and facial motion and the small gestures already permitted; it never changes framing or moves the head, shoulders, or torso toward the lens.

VISUAL AND COLOR CONSISTENCY:
Preserve <Subject 1>, <Subject 2>, and <Subject 3> continuously. WARDROBE LOCK: Keep the exact visible outer-to-inner layer order, garment colors and silhouette, sleeve and collar shapes, patterns, logo positions, and worn accessories from <Picture 1> throughout. BACKGROUND LOCK: Keep the same visible scene landmarks, image-left-to-right positions, relative depth, background blur, and existing objects; the scene contains only what is visible in <Picture 1>. COLOR & LIGHTING LOCK: Keep the original light direction, color temperature, white balance, exposure, saturation and skin tone stable without flicker or drift. Visual appearance never switches to the wardrobe or setting in <Video 1>.

SPEAKING PERFORMANCE:
From the first audible speech event, <Subject 1> (S1) speaks using <Audio 1> and says exactly:
<d>[Chinese] 有一次，一位开店的姐姐跟我说了一句话，我到现在都记得，她说，我这最重的一顿，总落在最晚。她早上六点多就起，先顾家里人，自己那份就算了；中午店里走不开，随便扒两口；晚上快九点才坐下来，吃一顿正经的饭。她说那阵子胃里总顶着，早上起来也不松快，那圈肉一直没动。家里人劝她早点吃，她说白天顾不上。然后她问我，徐博士，是不是我这年纪就这样了？她这个问题，不是一份食谱能解决的。</d> 
SPOKEN LINES ARE LIP-SYNC ONLY: Spoken words, numbers, transitions, and phrases are strictly phoneme timing data for lip articulation. The camera system MUST NOT treat any spoken words, transitions, or vocal volume shifts as cinematic directives or camera reframing triggers. Synchronize lips, mouth, jaw, cheeks, and chin to <Audio 1> phonemes, pauses, and delivery. Spoken dialogue is delivered through <Audio 1>; the spoken words are heard, not shown.

SPEECH FIDELITY:
Never produce speech content not present in <Audio 1>. During silent pauses keep mouth closed and face neutral. Before the first audible phoneme and after the final audible phoneme, lips rest closed and the jaw remains still. Facial emotion follows <Audio 1>. Use <Video 1> only for gaze, blinking, subtle non-speaking expressions and minor head motion.

MOTION BUDGET:
Keep movement small and speech-driven: lip motion, blinking, subtle breathing and minor head rotations. Maintain the visible posture and limb placement from <Picture 1>. restrained hand gestures are allowed only when hands are already clearly visible; hands stay near their starting positions and do not newly touch, move or cover scene objects. If hands are outside <Picture 1>, keep them out of frame. Keep the head, shoulders, and torso at the same depth as the opening throughout, including emphatic speech and the final seconds; avoid leaning, swaying, repeated bobbing or large pose changes.

SEGMENT CONTINUITY:
Maintain pose and identity through the final frame. After the last audible phoneme of <Audio 1>, lips stay closed and the jaw rests; only blinking and gentle breathing continue.

OUTPUT RESTRICTIONS:
The frame contains only <Subject 1>, <Subject 2>, and <Subject 3> exactly as in <Picture 1>, held in the same composition from the first frame to the last. Spoken dialogue is audio-only lip-sync guidance: add no subtitles, captions, lower-thirds, karaoke text, or transcript overlays. Preserve text and logos already visible on clothing or in the scene in <Picture 1>; do not create new on-screen words. Do not add cuts, transitions, fades, black frames, freeze frames, or end-of-clip effects.

overall_soundscape:
Speech follows <Audio 1>, with no newly introduced location-specific ambience or second speaker.

non_diegetic_music:
N/A
